## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Avivittakathā* (Kv 21.2) is an Abhidhamma debate belonging to the twenty-first chapter of the *Kathāvatthu* [Catalog]. As outlined by André Bareau, the discussion centers on the proposition that an ordinary person (*puthujjana*) is not separated or detached (*avivitta*) from the phenomena (*dhamma*) of the threefold world (*tedhātuka*) [Bareau 1955]. The thesis contends that because worldly dhammas are not fully comprehended (*apariññāta*) by an ordinary person, that person is not separated from them; this relates to the principle that phenomena are fixed in their own intrinsic nature (*sabhāva*) and never abandon (*vijahanti*) it, as in the case of material form (*rūpa*) remaining fixed in the nature of form [Bareau 1955].
